_comment: Structured concept model for adaptive learning. Kept as data, not code, so it can be edited and reviewed without touching Python. 'lesson_id' links a concept to its Markdown lesson in mentorsmith/lessons/. Prerequisites must be listed before the concepts that depend on them; core/concepts.py validates this and detects cycles.

concepts.title: Program Structure
concepts.summary: The entry point, includes, namespaces, statements and exit status.

concepts.title: Variables and Scope
concepts.summary: Declaring, initialising and constraining variables, and where they live.

concepts.title: Types and Integer Division
concepts.summary: Choosing int versus double and recognising truncated division.

concepts.title: Input and Output
concepts.summary: Reading with cin and getline, writing with cout, and checking input succeeded.

concepts.title: Operators and Precedence
concepts.summary: Arithmetic, comparison and short-circuit logic.

concepts.title: Conditions
concepts.summary: Branching correctly, ordering specific tests first, switch and break.

concepts.title: Loops
concepts.summary: while, do while and for, plus off-by-one reasoning and loop termination.

concepts.title: Functions
concepts.summary: Parameters, return values, pass by value versus reference.

concepts.title: Arrays and Vectors
concepts.summary: Fixed-size storage, indexing from zero, and bounds safety.

concepts.title: Strings
concepts.summary: std::string operations and safe access.

concepts.title: Pointers
concepts.summary: Addresses, dereferencing, null checks and never dereferencing uninitialised memory.

concepts.title: References
concepts.summary: Aliases, pass by reference, dangling references.

concepts.title: Memory Management
concepts.summary: Stack versus heap, leaks, double free, RAII and smart pointers.

concepts.title: Structures
concepts.summary: Grouping data, member access, passing structs to functions.

concepts.title: Classes and Objects
concepts.summary: Encapsulating state with member functions and const correctness.

concepts.title: Constructors and RAII
concepts.summary: Initialising objects safely, rule of zero, validating invariants.

concepts.title: File Handling
concepts.summary: Opening, checking, reading and writing files safely.

concepts.title: Exceptions and Errors
concepts.summary: Throwing, catching in the right order, and letting RAII clean up.

concepts.title: Inheritance and Derived Classes
concepts.summary: Deriving a class, constructor order, access under inheritance, and the diamond problem.

concepts.title: Operator Overloading
concepts.summary: Giving an operator a meaning for your own type, as a member or a free function.

concepts.title: Virtual Functions and Abstract Classes
concepts.summary: Choosing the body at run time, and building an abstract class from pure virtual functions.

projects.title: Number Guessing Game
projects.purpose: Practise loops, conditions and input validation by building a small interactive game.

milestones.title: Ask and validate
milestones.requirements: Prompt for a guess, read it as an int, and reject non-numeric input with a clear message.
acceptance_criteria: Program compiles with -Wall and no errors
Non-numeric input produces a helpful message and re-prompts
Exactly one value is read per iteration
milestones.hint: Test the stream: if (!(std::cin >> guess)) then handle it. Consider how you clear the bad state before re-reading.

milestones.title: Feedback loop
milestones.requirements: Tell the user whether the guess is too high, too low, or correct, and keep going until correct.
acceptance_criteria: Correct guess exits the loop
High and low guesses give distinct messages
Loop always terminates when the number is guessed
milestones.hint: A while loop with a bool 'solved' flag, or a do while, both work. Pick one and make the exit condition obvious.

milestones.title: Attempts and scoring
milestones.requirements: Count guesses and report the final count.
acceptance_criteria: Counter starts at 0 and increments once per guess
Final count is printed on exit
Count is correct for a scripted sequence
milestones.hint: Increment the counter immediately after a validated read, not inside the rejection path.

extensions: Cap the number of attempts and report a loss.
Let the player choose difficulty by narrowing a range.
Track a best score across runs using a file.

projects.title: Marks Analyser
projects.purpose: Practise arrays, loops and functions by turning a list of marks into statistics.

milestones.title: Read into a vector
milestones.requirements: Read a count then that many marks into a std::vector<int>, rejecting non-numeric input.
acceptance_criteria: Marks are stored in a vector, not a fixed array
Count and marks agree
Bad input is reported rather than silently accepted
milestones.hint: Read the count first, then loop with push_back. Use .at(i) rather than operator[] while you are learning.

milestones.title: Compute statistics
milestones.requirements: Write separate functions returning the sum, mean, highest and lowest.
acceptance_criteria: Each statistic is its own named function
Mean is computed as a double, not truncated
Functions take const std::vector<int>& parameters
milestones.hint: Watch out for integer division in the mean: cast the total before dividing.

milestones.title: Grade distribution
milestones.requirements: Count how many marks fall into each grade band and print a summary.
acceptance_criteria: Grades are ordered most specific first
Every mark is counted exactly once
Output labels each band
milestones.hint: One pass with if / else if chains ordered from the highest threshold down.

extensions: Sort the marks and print the median.
Read marks from a CSV file instead of the keyboard.

projects.title: Library Manager
projects.purpose: Practise structs, classes and file handling by managing a catalogue on disk.

milestones.title: The Book struct
milestones.requirements: Define a struct or class holding id, title and author.
acceptance_criteria: Fields are private with accessors, or a struct used consistently
Construction leaves a valid object
Compiles with -Wall cleanly
milestones.hint: Start with a plain struct, then decide what should be hidden.

milestones.title: Load and save
milestones.requirements: Write the catalogue to a file and read it back, checking every stream operation.
acceptance_criteria: File open is checked and reported
Round trip preserves every record
A missing file produces a clear message, not a crash
milestones.hint: Separate records with a delimiter that cannot appear in a title, and parse with istringstream.

milestones.title: Search and report
milestones.requirements: Search by title and by author, reporting matches and misses.
acceptance_criteria: Search is case-insensitive
No match reports clearly
Search does not modify the catalogue
milestones.hint: Lowercase both sides before comparing. std::find may save you a loop.

extensions: Detect duplicate ids at load time.
Write results to a separate report file.

projects.title: Log Analyser
projects.purpose: Practise strings, file handling and error handling by parsing a messy log file.

milestones.title: Parse a line
milestones.requirements: Split one log line into level, timestamp and message.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed lines are skipped, not fatal
The parse is a separate function you can test
No substring arithmetic assumptions
milestones.hint: istringstream plus a known delimiter is usually simpler than manual index searching.

milestones.title: Aggregate counts
milestones.requirements: Count occurrences per level and find the most common error message.
acceptance_criteria: Counts match a hand-checked example
A file with zero matching lines is handled
Performance is acceptable for a large file
milestones.hint: A std::map for counts. For most-common, track a running maximum as you go.

milestones.title: Report with honest failures
milestones.requirements: Write a summary report, and throw a meaningful exception if the input file is unreadable.
acceptance_criteria: Unreadable input raises a descriptive exception
The caller catches it and reports it to the user
A partial parse is never presented as a complete one
milestones.hint: Throw std::runtime_error with the path in the message; catch it at main.

extensions: Detect repeated identical errors across the log.
Compare two log files and report new error types.

projects.title: Expense Tracker
projects.purpose: Practise classes, constructors and file handling by recording and totalling spending.

milestones.title: The Expense class
milestones.requirements: Create a class that validates its constructor arguments and rejects invalid state.
acceptance_criteria: Negative amounts are rejected in the constructor
No invalid object can be constructed
Const accessors are used for read-only queries
milestones.hint: Validate in the constructor and throw std::invalid_argument. A constructor must never leave a half-valid object.

milestones.title: Store and total
milestones.requirements: Hold a collection of expenses and total them, passing by const reference.
acceptance_criteria: Totals are correct for a scripted sequence
Collection is not copied on every call
Empty collection returns 0.0 rather than crashing
milestones.hint: std::accumulate, or a range-based loop taking const Expense&.

milestones.title: Monthly grouping
milestones.requirements: Group expenses by month and report totals per month.
acceptance_criteria: Each expense lands in exactly one group
Months with no expenses are simply absent
Report is sorted predictably
milestones.hint: A map keyed by 'YYYY-MM' sorts for you.

extensions: Add a category to each expense.
Persist to JSON-like text and reload.
